subject: Cross-region reserved slice for NiftyRetail pilot — exception & runway
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Cross-region reserved slice for NiftyRetail pilot — exception & runway

Team —

NiftyRetail (Caroline Ng) just committed to a two-week production-like pilot that starts the week of Feb 12. They want consistent low tail latency across US-WEST and EU-WEST during a simulated peak (concurrent storefront inference + nightly batch reindexes). Their ask: a small reserved slice in both regions for the first two weeks of the pilot to preserve KV cache warmness and avoid cold-start tails.

Key constraints from the customer:
- Pilot window: Feb 12–26 (two full weeks)
- Expected sustained qps at peak: ~420 qps across two regions (split ~65/35)
- Hard requirement: tail P99 latency below 350ms for storefront calls

Asking for help on three things:
1) Can we authorize a temporary carveout/reservation for us-west and eu-west (minimal slices) that bypasses the standard 14-day carveout notice?
2) What autoscale policy exception would we need to keep KV cache populated (low scale-down aggressiveness)?
3) Rough incremental cost estimate (chargeback to NiftyRetail or apply pilot credits) — I attached the rough traffic profile.

Attachment: nifty-pilot-runway.xlsx (spreadsheet, ~42KB) — contains per-hour qps profiles and model variant choices.

I know this bumps policy; opening this thread to get cross-functional alignment and a path we can present to the customer by EOD Monday.

Thanks —
Mateo
Product PM, Dedicated Capacity & Onboarding
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-region reserved slice for NiftyRetail pilot — exception & runway

+1 on wanting to move quickly. A few operating constraints to call out up front:

- Policy: standard carveout requires a 14-day lead time plus a signed commitment for reserved capacity. We can do an exception but need either (a) a commercial pre-commit or (b) an internal emergency waiver with clear rollback criteria.
- Autoscale exceptions we can toggle: max_scale_down_rate (to keep nodes warm), and short-circuit preemptible reclaim windows for the reserved pool. Both are doable but require ops lead time to schedule the slice in the allocator.

Questions for customer / product:
1) Can NiftyRetail sign a 2-week paid reservation (minimum $X/day), or do they expect this covered as part of pilot credits?
2) Which model variant are they pinning? If they want frequent model swaps across the pilot we can't guarantee pinned caches.

I attached a short excerpt of the carveout policy that lists the approval path and required procurement docs. If we want a one-week buffered approval (reduced from 14d), we should accept the following constraints: limited to a single model variant per region, strict burst caps, and an ops rollback at the midpoint.

Attachment: carveout-policy-extract.pdf (pdf, 9KB)

If product can get Caroline to confirm the signature path and model pinning today, I can get legal/procurement started and draft the waiver.

—Kimberly
Head of Dedicated Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 13:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-region reserved slice for NiftyRetail pilot — exception & runway

Thanks — operationally this is feasible with a few guardrails. High-level ops plan:

1) Reserve minimal slices: 4 GPUs (2 in us-west, 2 in eu-west) for the first 7 days; re-evaluate at day 7 and either extend to full two-week carveout or scale down. This gives us a safety-first option and buys time for procurement.
2) Autoscale tweak: set max_scale_down_rate to 0.2 for the reserved pool and enable prefix/KV sticky caching for pinned model variants.
3) Pre-warm: run the pre-warm script 6 hours before go-time with a controlled synthetic trace (we'll need token limits — see attached runbook).
4) Fallback: we will prepare a lighter quantized variant to route to if contention appears — this requires product sign-off to pin the serving config.

I created an internal Jira to track the carveout scheduling: INF-7421 (ops runbook + deployment windows). If procurement can push a short-term PO or waiver, we can schedule the reserve allocation in the next allocator roll (target window: Feb 10–11).

Attachment: ops-runbook-snapshot.md (text, 15KB) — contains pre-warm steps and rollback checklist.

Operational asks for product/procurement:
- Product: confirm pinned variant and whether quantized fallback is acceptable.
- Procurement: confirm whether customer signs a 2-week paid reservation or whether we issue a credit.

If we get those answers today, I can book the allocator window and pre-warm run.

—Jonas
SRE Lead, Dedicated Runtime
Redwood Inference

Finance/procurement here — provisional approval subject to terms below:

1) Commercial: we can approve a short-term paid reservation for the two-week window, billed at the pilot daily rate. If NiftyRetail insists on credits, they must accept a smaller reserved footprint (single-region or single-slate).
2) Contract: we need a signed pilot addendum that includes an SLA addendum for the reserved lanes and an explicit rollback clause. Legal will prepare the addendum once Product confirms model pin and region split.
3) Risk controls: internal waiver approved only if ops confirms pre-warm + rollback checklist (Jonas, you flagged INF-7421 — good).

I estimate incremental cost to NiftyRetail at $7,800 (two-week minimal slices across both regions, including warm cache overhead). I'll open a purchase order template and a short-term invoice if Caroline confirms commercial path.

Action items:
- Product (Mateo): get customer confirmation on pinning model and signature path today.
- Ops (Jonas): finalize pre-warm schedule in INF-7421 and share runbook.
- Legal/Procurement: I'll draft addendum and PO template on receipt of customer signature.

I'll mark this as priority and loop in Legal once Product shares the signatory contact.

—Neha
Sr. Manager, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
